title: Manus Formally Resumes Independent Operations, Ending Meta's $2 Billion Acquisition More Than Four Months After Beijing Blocked It
detail: Manus, the Chinese-founded AI agent startup, announced on Tuesday, September 1, that it had formally resumed independent operations under its original founding team, completing the unwind of Meta's roughly $2 billion acquisition after China's National Development and Reform Commission ordered the deal reversed on national-security grounds in late April. Meta and Manus completed an operational and data split earlier in the summer, erasing user data generated after the December 29, 2025 acquisition date and requiring users to restore data through a dedicated portal; Manus now stores data in the US and Singapore rather than under Meta's systems. Investors including Tencent, ZhenFund and Sequoia-linked HSG purchased Manus shares from Meta as part of the unwind, with Tencent positioned to become the largest shareholder. Manus said its annualized recurring revenue grew from $100 million in December 2025 to $400 million by late June 2026. The reversal is the first instance of Beijing using its foreign-investment security review mechanism to force a US tech giant to divest a Chinese-founded AI company, and sets a precedent for cross-border AI acquisitions involving Chinese talent.

media.caption: AI agent start-up Manus has resumed independent operations after unwinding its acquisition by Meta Platforms

title: Zhipu AI (Z.ai) First-Half 2026 Revenue Surges Nearly 400% to $134M as API Business Grows 27-Fold
detail: Zhipu AI (Z.ai), the Beijing-based large-language-model developer, reported first-half 2026 revenue of 954 million yuan (~$134 million), up 399.7% year-on-year, in results covered by Caixin Global on September 1. The growth was driven almost entirely by its open-platform and API business, which surged 27.4-fold to 825 million yuan and now accounts for 86.5% of total revenue, up from just 15.2% a year earlier, as enterprise customers shifted from buying general-purpose models to consuming Zhipu's GLM models via cloud API. Annualized recurring revenue reached $1.6 billion as of August, roughly double rival MiniMax's, while token calls on the platform rose more than 40-fold since early 2026 across 7.4 million enterprise and developer users. Net loss narrowed 12.1% to 2.07 billion yuan, and the cloud-deployment business achieved gross profitability at a 24.6% margin versus -0.4% a year earlier — evidence Zhipu is beginning to convert scale into unit economics even as it continues to operate large training and inference clusters on domestically produced Huawei Ascend chips amid US export restrictions.

media.caption: Zhipu AI's first-half 2026 revenue rose nearly 400% year-on-year as its API and cloud business took off
